transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hey, good to meet you too. Um, so what brought me in... well, I basically went from just being a normal crew guy on the landscaping team to suddenly trying to run three different bids all at once. I was calling city council people, trying to line up all these wholesale plant suppliers... which, man, getting a hold of decent Japanese maples right now is a total nightmare. There's this huge shortage because of some fungus out west, or at least that's what my buddy Mike says. Mike drives a rig for a nursery, we actually went to high school together, played baseball. We weren't very good, but we had a blast. We made it to regionals once, though, and I hit a double in the ninth inning. 

Anyway, what was I... oh, right. Yeah, so I was doing all that and just messaging everybody I knew about this massive new park idea I had. It was just non-stop, like I couldn't shut it off, you know? Just constantly going.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don't seem to?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, my hearing is actually really sharp, though. Way better than my boss, Dave. Dave is practically deaf in his left ear from running the wood chipper without ear protection back in the 90s. I keep telling him, you gotta wear the muffs, man. The heavy-duty Stihl ones, not those cheap little foam plugs. The foam ones just fall out the second you start sweating, and man, we were sweating buckets last Tuesday pulling out this massive old juniper bush. Juniper is the absolute worst, it's so prickly and it gets right through your gloves. I had scratches all up and down my forearms, looked like I got into a fight with a bobcat. 

But yeah, no, I don't hear or see... like, imaginary stuff, if that's what you're asking. Just the regular stuff.
Before this started, had you been using any drugs or stimulants like meth, cocaine, Adderall, or a lot of energy drinks?

No, no drugs. I mean, I don't mess with meth or cocaine or any of that. Adderall, no. Energy drinks... well, I mean, I'll have a coffee in the morning, but that's about it. Dave, though, my boss, he drinks those Monster energy drinks like water. The green ones. I don't know how his heart hasn't exploded yet, honestly. He buys them by the case at Costco. Have you been to Costco lately? It's a madhouse. You can't even get down the aisles on a Saturday. My wife wanted me to go pick up some of those bulk paper towels, the Kirkland brand, because they're actually thicker than Bounty, believe it or not. But I told her, I'm not going near that place on a weekend. The parking lot alone is a nightmare. People just backing out without even looking. I almost got T-boned by a minivan last month right by the food court exit. The guy was just staring at his phone. 

But yeah, no drugs or anything for me. Just coffee.
Have you felt like you have special powers or an important mission that other people would find unrealistic?

Special powers? Nah, no magic or anything. But a mission... yeah, kinda. I honestly believed I was about to become the guy that every single town around here called for sustainable landscaping. Like, the absolute top expert everyone needed. Which is pretty funny looking back, because realistically, I’m still just trying to keep my small jobs paid up. 

Getting people to actually pay their invoices on time is like pulling teeth, man. I use this app on my phone to send the bills, but it updated last week and now all the buttons are moved around. I hate when they do that. Just leave the app alone, you know? It's exactly like how they changed the recipe for those barbecue chips I like. They slap "new and improved" on the bag, but it's never improved. It just tastes way saltier. I used to eat a whole bag of those after a long shift of mowing, just sitting on the tailgate of my truck. My truck's got like 200,000 miles on it, by the way. Chevy Silverado. Still runs like a dream, mostly. The AC is completely busted, but you just roll the windows down. Though, driving on the highway with the windows down means you can't even hear the radio, and the speakers are already kind of blown out from when I used to blast Metallica in my early twenties... wait, what did you ask me again? Something about the landscaping?
How many days in a row did this nonstop, high-energy period last?

Well, that whole fired-up, overconfident stretch... it started right when I began remaking myself for that big park pitch, you know? And it kept going for about two weeks before I just completely crashed. Two weeks of just... go, go, go. Which is wild because usually by Thursday I'm pretty beat. 

Thursdays are when we do the municipal routes, mowing all the medians down on Route 9. People drive like absolute maniacs on that road. I saw a guy in a silver BMW literally hop the curb to get around a garbage truck last month. Blew out his front passenger tire instantly. Serves him right, honestly. Those low-profile tires they put on luxury cars are completely useless anyway. Hit one decent pothole and you're out a thousand bucks. My buddy Greg runs a tire shop over on 4th street, and he says he makes half his rent just replacing rims for guys who think they're driving in the Indy 500. Greg's a good guy, though, he actually helped me install a new alternator in my truck last year. Took us like six hours because we kept stopping to grill hot dogs and mess with his dog. He's got this massive Rottweiler mix that just wants to play fetch with tennis balls all day, but he destroys them in like two bites. 

But wait, what did you ask me? The energy thing? Yeah, about two weeks, I'd say.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah, man. I mean, honestly, this whole depressed thing has been hanging over me for about a year now. But this latest crash? It's the absolute worst it's ever gotten. I can barely drag myself out of bed most days. 

Which is a real problem because my mattress is completely shot anyway. It's got this massive dip right in the middle, like a crater. I keep telling myself I'm gonna go to that mattress liquidator place out on Route 22, but I never do. You know the guy in their commercials? The one who yells about slashing prices and wears that ridiculous foam crown? I actually saw him at a diner once. Just eating a turkey club, totally normal guy, no crown. It was almost disappointing, you know? Like finding out Santa Claus isn't real. My little nephew just figured that out last Christmas. He's seven, smart kid, loves dinosaurs. He can name like fifty different kinds of dinosaurs. The other day he was trying to explain to me the difference between a Brachiosaurus and an Apatosaurus, and I'm just sitting there like, buddy, they both look like giant green giraffes to me. 

But yeah, what were we talking about? The depression? Yeah, it's been about a year, but this crash right now is just brutal.
